lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 20, which makes a double-click on empty space open the parent folder, as in Nemo.
It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
It starts with a left double-click on blank space, with no Ctrl, Shift or Alt held.
lines.say: It starts with a left double-click on blank space, with no control, shift or alt key held.

lines.caption: On each left press, the view checks whether an item or a row is under the pointer.
A shared helper checks that both presses hit blank space in the same folder, and that the preference is on.
Then it runs the existing Open Parent action. At the top folder, that does nothing.
A checkbox on the Behavior tab of Preferences turns it off.
The checkbox is bound to a new xfconf setting, which is on by default.
lines.say: The checkbox is bound to a new X F conf setting, which is on by default.

lines.caption: Nemo goes up a folder on a double-click in empty space. Thunar only had the Up button and Alt+Up.
lines.say: Nemo goes up a folder on a double-click in empty space. Thunar only had the Up button and alt up.

lines.caption: In split view, the pane you click is already the active one, so the double-click acts on that pane.
Step one: the single presses are only noted, never consumed, so clicks and rubber-band selection work as before.
Step two: the icon and compact views ask for the item under the pointer; the details view reuses its row lookup.
Step three: the helper counts blank presses in a row, and acts only when both hit blank space in one folder.
Step four calls Open Parent the same way the swipe-up gesture already does, so there is no new go-up code.
Step five: the checkbox sits right under Double click to activate items, in the Navigation section.
Step six: the helper reads the setting on every double-click, so a change applies at once, without a restart.
Blank space in any view opens the parent folder. In split view, only the pane you clicked goes up.
At the top folder, with the checkbox off, or with a modifier key held, nothing happens.
Single-click mode is left alone, because there a click can open an item before the double-click completes.
A double-click on a file or folder opens it as before, and column headers are unchanged.
The PR changes the three views, the shared helper, the preferences and their dialog, and adds a verify script.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It was built on the existing Open Parent action, and checked against each line of issue 3.
It built as a Debian package with no new warnings, and the PR's CI run was green on all four jobs.
A verify script double-clicked blank space in all three views and in both split-view panes, and the folder went up.
A double-click on a folder still opened it and stayed there, also in single-click mode.
Rubber-band selection still worked, and at the top folder nothing happened and no dialog opened.
Unticking the checkbox turned it off at once, and an independent audit passed all the screenshots.
Whether the setting survives a restart of Thunar was not tested.
A fresh local agent found three low findings. CI's review then found two medium ones, and both were fixed.
The main fix: a folder opened by the first click no longer counts as blank space, so it can't bounce you back.
How it feels in your own session, and the split-view crash check, can only be tried after the merge.
Part 3. What comes later: nothing depends on issue 3.
After the merge, try it in each view and in split view, and run the manual split-view crash check.
That's the tour: a double-click on empty space now takes you up one folder, and one checkbox turns it off.
